title: Magnetic Levitation Coupled with Portable Imaging and Analysis for Disease Diagnostics
protocol: Prepare a 50 mM solution of gadobutrol in Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS).
Dissolve 10 mM sodium metabisulfite in the gadolinium solution.
Obtain blood sample via fingerstick or venipuncture.
Draw blood using a lancing device with a clean, disposable lancet.
Apply pressure near the pierced site and wipe the blood droplet formed three to four times before collecting blood using a pipette.
Add less than 1 μL of blood to 100 μl of the gadolinium-sodium metabisulfite solution.
Lyse RBCs with an RBC lysis buffer.
Pipette 5 µL of blood into 500 µL of RBC lysis buffer.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 3 - 5 min.
Dilute whole blood 1:1,000 in 25 mM Gd in HBSS.
If cell lysis was performed, dilute the lysed sample 9:1 lysed sample:250 mM Gd to obtain a sample containing 25 mM Gd.
Start the magnetic levitation device by plugging it into an outlet and allowing it to power up.
Place the device on a flat, level surface for use.
Load the prepared sample into a square glass microcapillary tube by dipping the end into the solution and allowing the sample to fill via capillary action.
Seal one end of the capillary with a tube sealant by slowly pushing it in.
Insert the sealed capillary between the magnets so that only 1 cm remains visible.
Wait 10 min without disturbing the device or the capillary.
Load the sample into the sample tube.
Connect the inlet tubing between the sample container and microcapillary.
Connect the outlet tubing between the microcapillary and waste container.
Set the LED intensity and flow parameters.
Ensure that cells are visible in the field of view, then press the capture button to capture an image.
If a USB is used to store the images, create a folder called "images" and insert the USB prior to turning on the device.
Capture several images by moving the capillary in or out about ½ cm between each capturing.
If the number of cells within the field of view is too high or too low, shift the capillary in or out of the device or prepare another sample.
Remove the sample and discard it according to institutional or local regulations.
Observe the output of the analysis displayed on-screen.
Record the width of confinement for cell distribution analysis, such as sickle cell disease diagnosis.
For cell type separation, such as WBC identification, record an image with the WBC population identified.
Calculate the number of cells per microliter by multiplying the average number of WBCs per image by a factor of 2,000.
Repeat the analysis by moving the sample tube in or out of the device about ½ cm and capturing another image for analysis.
Repeat the analysis 5 - 6 times per sample to avoid errors.
